build.summary:
I built access-multi-site: one full case can now hold several access sites, and each site has its own puncture model, wire route, sheath, closure and delayed events. The fields the rest of the lab already read (access, site, pm, route, sheath, radial, femoral, delayed and the radial closure results) are now getters and setters on the active site. addSite(kind, side) works after the planned site has been punctured: radial artery of either arm, or femoral artery or vein of either groin. setActiveSite only switches with the wire and catheter out. closureDone() and finish() need every site that had a sheath to be closed. Each site draws its delayed events on its own seed, and a scenario's delayed events are added once per case, so no bleed is counted twice. buildRoute3D accepts a left groin (the right limb mirrored across the midline), and the femoral angiogram's branches now mirror for the left groin. truth() and the handover note list every site and line. The new scenario 'crossover-heparinised' opens a heparinised radial case at fluoroscopy with the wire unable to pass. A heparinised femoral crossover records a ledger decision that counts as expected only when the artery was imaged on ultrasound and the groin screened on fluoroscopy before the needle. In the UI there is a site selector on the ultrasound, fluoroscopy and closure views, an 'Another site…' control in the access picker, a venous-sheath closure button, and a sites-and-lines field in the handover.

How the work happened: the lead's note said the first attempt failed before doing any work, but its transcript shows it had already written most of the simulation layer (caseSession.ts, route.ts, procedure.ts, autopilot.ts, the crossover scenario and both multiSite test files) before a network error stopped it. I deleted its snapshot folder before I noticed this. I rebuilt the true pre-work snapshot from that attempt's own full reads of the four files it edited; the line counts (2415, 518, 391, 294) match its own wc output. datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/access-multi-site/NOTE.txt records this. I kept its work after reviewing it rather than starting over, and then finished the UI and fixed two things in the scoring.

build.notes:
Earlier attempt and snapshot: transcript agent-ab31c974382b09604 (workflow wf_7cf449bd-b7a) did roughly 85 tool calls of real work before the network error, so the build lead's note was mistaken. I deleted its 12:33 snapshot folder before noticing. The snapshot now holds the true pre-package state, rebuilt from that attempt's full reads of caseSession.ts, route.ts, procedure.ts and autopilot.ts. The UI files and caseSession.test.ts were never touched by it (their modification times predate it), so the copies taken now are the originals. crossover.ts and crossover.launch.ts did not exist before the package. NOTE.txt in the snapshot folder explains this for reviewers.

Changes I made on top of the earlier work:
1. Per-site probeOn state, with setProbeOn(). It is on at the planned site, so existing behaviour is unchanged, and off at an added site. Without it, the view's per-frame image report would have marked every crossover as ultrasound-guided, because the needle is placed from inside the ultrasound view.
2. The crossover decision now needs both ultrasound and fluoroscopy, matching the tip text. The autopilot's crossover() takes ultrasound and fluoroscopy options. It records a groin screening without booking any dose.
3. The femoral angiogram's SFA and PFA offsets are mirrored for the left groin; they were hard-coded for the right.
4. All of the UI work.

Fluoroscopy view: the limb anatomy is rebuilt lazily when the active site's route changes, so the renderer and the dose meter are not recreated, and the table goes back to the new route's first station.

Closure panel: it moves to Recovery only once no other site is still open.

Handover: it offers all six site and side combinations, so the list does not reveal which sites were used.

The site selector marks a site 'closed' only after the learner has closed it themselves; it shows no other answer.

Design choices to review: an added left groin uses its own anatomy seed (`${seed}:left-groin`). A femoral vein site reuses the groin anatomy with the vein (cfv) as the target, and it is closed by taking the sheath out and holding pressure.

siteSelector.test.ts mocks useProcedureStore with a plain selector hook, because a server render of a zustand store reads its initial state, which has no session.

review.verdict: The package mostly meets its plan, but one engine bug needs fixing before it is accepted (accept after fixes). The design is implemented: per-site state behind getters on the active site, addSite and setActiveSite, closureDone() across all sites, the left-groin mirror in route.ts, a per-site delayed-event seed with scenario events added once, a site list in truth() and the handover, the crossover-heparinised scenario and launch file, and a selector on the ultrasound, fluoroscopy and closure views. I ran the checks myself. The three package test files pass (25/25). caseSession.test.ts is byte-identical to its snapshot, and caseSession, scenarios, handover, ledgerTips, procedure and access tests pass (81/81). npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit is clean. caseTips.reach.test.ts fails 1 of 42. That failure comes from another package: waiting.ts lines 512-517 now put the cold-leg tips under access-cx-endovascular-control. The tests are meaningful and cover every non-browser acceptance item. Requiring both ultrasound and fluoroscopy before the crossover puncture is correct: lab request pm-antithrombotics#7 asks for 'ultrasound and fluoroscopy guided', and so does the tip text. Shared engines keep their defaults (buildRoute3D's side parameter is optional and defaults to right; the right femoral lateral and the angiogram offsets are unchanged). One-site behaviour is unchanged: the per-site band threshold expression is the same as catheterFr(). I found no unsourced clinical numbers and no ground truth on live screens. The UI uses existing Clinical Graphite classes and British English. Every src file newer than .started that is not in the package list belongs to another package's file list (tips.ts, waiting.ts, content.test.ts, mentor/*, Settings*, physics/types.test.ts). Two things are left open. The browser criterion was not checked in the browser; siteSelector.test.ts covers it only headlessly. The four rebuilt snapshot files cannot be checked independently, although every diff hunk is coherent multi-site work.

findings.problem: Femoral closure runs afterClosure() in a deferred spend callback, so it acts on whichever site is active when the time lapse ends. setActiveSite() does not check this.busy. I reproduced it in a scratch test: crossover-heparinised, crossover(s,'right'), s.femoralManual(15,3) (busy true), s.setActiveSite(radialId) returns true, then runPending(). Result: the radial sheath is set to null without any closure, the femoral site gets no delayed events and no sheathHistory, and closureDone() stays false, so the case cannot be finished. The UI's selector is disabled while busy, which hides this in the app, but the session API itself corrupts state.
findings.fix: Add a busy guard at the top of setActiveSite: `if (this.busy) { this.say("Wait for the step in hand to finish.", "technique"); return false; }`. Also bind the closure to its site. In femoralManual and femoralDevice capture `const site = this.activeSite`, and pass `() => this.afterClosure(site)` to spend. Then make afterClosure(site = this.activeSite) read and write site.delayed, site.closure.femoral, site.closure.radial and site.sheath (or set this.activeIdx = this.sites.indexOf(site) while it runs) instead of the active-site getters. Add a multiSite.test.ts case: femoralManual, then setActiveSite(radial) is refused (or the closure still lands on the femoral site), and the radial sheath is still in.

findings.where: src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts truth() (one-site fallback when sites.length > 1 but fewer than two sites had a sheath)
findings.problem: The fallback reads this.access, this.sheath and this.femoral from the active site. addSiteBlocked() allows a new site after closure (the plan's 'opposite groin for a bleed' path). If that site gets no sheath, truth() describes the empty new site. I reproduced it: radial case fastForward to recovery, then addSite('femoral','right'). truth() returns {site:'femoral', sheath:'', closure:'manual'}, while finish() reports access 'radial-right' with the 6 Fr sheath. A correct handover note is then graded wrong on site, sheath and closure.
findings.fix: In truth(), when this.sites.length > 1, take the one-site fields from `const one = used[0] ?? this.workingSite()` and not from the active site: site: one.route, sheath: one.sheath?.id ?? one.sheathHistory, closure from one.closure.femoral or 'radial-band', and bandOffHours from one.closure.bandHours when one.siteKind === 'radial'. Add a test: add a site after closure without puncturing it, then truth() still names the radial site.

findings.problem: The 'Puncture the planned site first' rule checks the active site, not the planned one. After the learner adds a site and before puncturing it, any further addSite is refused with a message about the planned site, which is wrong. One example is a femoral vein beside a just-added femoral artery; another is correcting a wrong-side choice. An unused added site also can never be removed, so it stays in every selector and switches the handover to its multi-site layout.
findings.fix: Apply the rule to this.sites[0]: `const p = this.sites[0]; if (this.sites.length === 1 && p.pm.st.passes === 0 && !p.sheath) return 'Puncture the planned site first; ...'`. Keep the midPuncture check for the active site. Optionally add removeSite(id) for an added site with pm.st.passes === 0 and no sheath.

findings.where: src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts noteProbeImage() (called every B-mode frame from src/ui/access/UltrasoundView.tsx)
findings.problem: This runs in the ultrasound render loop at up to 30 frames/s. Each call allocates a closure for st.site.tubes.find and a tubeAt() result, and it keeps working after usImagedAt is already set. That breaks the rule against per-frame allocations in render paths, and the view ignores the return value.
findings.fix: Cache the target tube on AccessSiteState in makeSite (e.g. `target: site.tubes.find(t => t.id === site.arteryId) ?? null`). In noteProbeImage, return early with `if (!st.probeOn) return false; if (st.usImagedAt !== null) return true;` before the geometry. The view keeps calling it unchanged.

findings.where: src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts removeSheathAndCompress() at a femoral-vein site
findings.problem: At a femoral vein site, `planned = st.siteKind === 'femoral-vein'` treats any sheath as a correct venous closure. A sheath that went into the artery (sheath.venous false; flushSheath says 'This sheath is in the artery, not the vein') is pulled under 'Pull the venous sheath and hold pressure' with no complication or ledger entry. A venous-site closure also emits no 'closure' event, unlike arterial closures.
findings.fix: Use `const planned = st.siteKind === 'femoral-vein' && wasVenous;`. For an arterial sheath at a vein site, record a minor complication (an existing id, or a new MODEL-labelled one). Emit `this.emit('closure', { delayed: [], site: st.id })` when a venous site closes, so the tip context sees each site's closure.

fix.notes:
I checked each finding against the code before changing anything. Five were correct and are fixed. The other two need files outside this package.

Files changed:
- /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts
- /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/access/panels/HandoverPanel.tsx
- /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/simulation/session/multiSite.test.ts

1. **Closure acting on the wrong site (major).** `setActiveSite()` now refuses to switch while a timed step is running, with "Wait for the step in hand to finish."
   - `femoralManual()` and `femoralDevice()` now record which site they started at and pass it to `afterClosure(site)`.
   - `afterClosure` makes that site active while it does the closure work (split out into a new `drawClosure(site)`). It then puts the previous active site back before `onSiteClosed` runs.
   - A new test checks the switch is refused. It also forces the active site to move during the compression and checks the closure still lands on the femoral site, with the radial sheath still in.

2. **truth() describing an empty added site.** When the case has more than one site but fewer than two had a sheath, truth() now describes `used[0] ?? workingSite()` instead of the active site. That covers access site, sheath, closure, band-off time and checks.
   - The helper `lastSheath()` was no longer used, so I removed it.
   - A new test adds a site after closure and checks truth() still names the radial site, its sheath and the band.

3. **"Puncture the planned site first" checked the wrong site.** The rule now applies only to the planned site, and only while it is the case's only site. The mid-puncture check still applies to the active site.
   - A new test adds a femoral vein site while an added femoral artery site is still unpunctured.
   - I did not add the optional `removeSite()`. It would need new UI, which the review did not ask for.

4. **Allocation in the ultrasound render loop.** Each site now stores its target vessel once, in a new field `AccessSiteState.target`.
   - `noteProbeImage()` returns false at once when the probe is off. It returns true at once when the vessel has already been imaged, without redoing the geometry.
   - One behaviour change: after the first image it keeps returning true even if the probe moves away. Nothing in the app or autopilot uses the return value, and the doc comment now says this.
   - A new test covers this.

5. **Arterial sheath at a femoral vein site.** Pulling a sheath at a vein site now counts as the venous closure only if the sheath was in the vein.
   - A sheath that went into the artery is removed as a misplaced sheath: the site stays open and no sheath is recorded for the handover.
   - It records a new minor complication, `arterial-sheath-at-vein`, labelled MODEL PARAMETER in the code. I added it to the handover's complication list so the learner can report it.
   - A venous-site closure now emits a closure event naming the site, like arterial closures do.
   - Two new tests cover the misplaced sheath and the venous closure event.

Not fixed here:
- **Finding 6:** the build lead needs to add a docs/realism/facts entry for `WIRE_STALL_MM`.
- **Finding 7:** the caseTips.reach.test.ts failure belongs to whoever owns that test or waiting.ts.

problems.problem: After the radial catheter came out and a femoral site was added, the guided readout on the new site's fluoroscopy view said 'abdominal aorta · wire 166 mm' with no wire in the body. removeCatheter() leaves wire.pos at the radial value (166 mm), and the readout maps that onto the new site's femoral route. In a one-site case the stale number was harmless; with several sites it names the wrong vessel at the wrong site.
problems.fix: In AccessFluoroView, render the readout and TipDial only when s.wireInBody, i.e. `{readouts && s.wireInBody && (...)}`. Alternatively, reset `this.wire = initialWire()` in removeCatheter() or in setActiveSite()/addSite() (both in caseSession.ts, this package's file).

problems.where: src/simulation/session/scenarios/crossover.ts (header comment) and the launch link in crossover.launch.ts
problems.problem: The scenario's comment says 'Nothing on screen names the loop or says the radial route has failed'. The case opens in guided mode, though, and the guided fluoroscopy readout shows 'radial loop · wire 166 mm · catheter 151 mm', which names the loop. Guided aids are allowed to show ground truth, so this breaks no rule, but the comment does not match what the learner sees.
problems.fix: Either change the comment to say that only the guided readout names the segment, or, if the loop should stay hidden, add `mode` to the link params in crossover.launch.ts (e.g. params: { workspace: 'fluoro', mode: '<unguided mode id>' }) so the readout is off.

rejected: Finding 3 (thin vertical line at the LEFT groin and pelvis): not fixed in this package, because the cause is outside its files. I traced it in the running app. Removing all 12 limbExtras primitives left the line in place, and so did moving the dummy catheter nodes. Switching off only the table hardware (buildXrayScene hardware with table:false) removed it at the pelvis station: the line at columns 239-241 disappeared. The line is the 1.5 mm carbon-fibre end wall of the table top in src/render/xray/hardware.ts, at world x = +/-229.25 mm, which is 40 mm deep and 2400 mm long. It falls inside the field because toWorld (src/simulation/anatomy.ts) rotates the whole aortic-frame route about the aortic root by the aortic tilt. That moves the caudal limb roughly 200 mm towards the patient's left in world coordinates. The camera centre sat at world x of about 278 at the left groin (aortic x 80) and about 215 at the left pelvis, so the left groin lies beyond the table edge. The right groin, at world x of about 130, does not. The x varies from case to case because the tilt and the groin position vary with the patient. Fixing it means making the limb route and limb extras compensate for the render-only aortic tilt, or placing the table relative to the tilted pelvis. That belongs to the anatomy, render or hardware owner, or to the femoral-site package that is planned to rework limbExtras (lab-build-plan.json around line 4114), not to this package.
